about: Category rules every gearbox's variables file must follow, so the same kind of variable gets the same category in every gearbox type. A variable whose name matches a pattern must have that category and sub-type (tests/test_variable_categories.py). Add the names a new gearbox uses for the same role to the pattern when that gearbox is classified. A rule can list exceptions per gearbox ("except": {gearbox: [names]}) where the same name plays a different role, e.g. INWPG's fw_p_b is a copy of fw_r_b (the reverse of WPG) and INCPG's fw_r is its stress width plus one clearance (fw_r_stress).

rules.reason: ring-gear teeth are implicitly constrained: the coaxial geometric constraint (e.g. Nr = Ns + 2 x Np) fixes them once the sun and planet teeth are chosen, so the optimiser sets them instead of searching them

gear face widths follow from the tooth-stress rule: the optimisation variables, the motor torque, the gear material and the safety factors fix them, and the optimiser always takes the smallest width that passes (widths that are a formula of another width, e.g. CPG's fw_p_s = fw_r + clearance_planet, are dependent / formula)

the same stress-rule face widths in a two-stage gearbox, under the stage prefixes a1_ / a2_ (the planet width a1_fw_p / a2_fw_p is a copy of the ring width, so it is dependent / formula and not in this rule)
